title: Exact cell-gain fits need a 33.52-fold role range in 28 selected WT and unc-31 worm responses
abstract: We tested bounded cell gains for changes in response magnitude between WT and unc-31 worms. A prior 28-pair sample forms a forest and admits exact fits with free source and target gains. We find that exact fits require a maximum-to-minimum range of at least 33.516 in one role. Allowing each response mean to change by factor 1.10 lowers the minimum range to 15.635; factor 1.25 lowers it to 5.623. An independent four-edge path bound matches all three optima. Stricter selection lowers the exact-fit range to 2.528 or 2.944. Linear programs, primal-dual checks and synthetic cases support the calculations. No gain calibration or response error bound was measured. These are conditional sensitivity results, not evidence for a synaptic or strain mechanism. Selected pooled means, different animals and separate role gains limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Minimum cell-role gain range versus allowed multiplicative change per response mean. Selections overlap; no measured error factor is inferred.
